## Introduction

In this task, you estimated:

1. **60 seconds** of time (without counting)
2. **Line lengths** in centimeters
3. **String lengths** in centimeters

Humans are notoriously bad at estimating time - we tend to either **overestimate** (think time passes faster) or **underestimate** (think time passes slower).

::: {.key-finding}
#### Key Finding
On average, participants estimated **55 seconds** when asked to mark 60 seconds, showing a slight tendency to underestimate time duration.
:::

## Time Estimation Accuracy

How close were participants to 60 seconds?

```{webr-r}
# Calculate error from target
timewarp <- timewarp |>
  mutate(
    error = estimate - 60,
    abs_error = abs(error)
  )

# Summary statistics
timewarp |>
  summarise(
    mean_estimate = mean(estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_error = mean(error, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_abs_error = mean(abs_error, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

## Visualise Time Estimates

```{webr-r}
ggplot(timewarp, aes(x = estimate)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 3, fill = "#f39c12", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 60, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "#275882", linewidth = 1.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 62, y = 3, label = "Target: 60s",
           hjust = 0, color = "#275882", size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    x = "Time Estimate (seconds)",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Time Estimation Performance",
    subtitle = "How close to 60 seconds?"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "#275882")
  )
```

## Over or Underestimation?

```{webr-r}
# Classify each estimate
timewarp <- timewarp |>
  mutate(
    estimation_type = case_when(
      error > 5 ~ "Overestimate",
      error < -5 ~ "Underestimate",
      TRUE ~ "Accurate (±5s)"
    )
  )

ggplot(timewarp, aes(x = estimation_type, fill = estimation_type)) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Accurate (±5s)" = "#27ae60",
                                "Overestimate" = "#e74c3c",
                                "Underestimate" = "#3498db")) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Count",
    title = "Time Estimation Patterns",
    subtitle = "Did participants over- or under-estimate?"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold")
  )
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## What Does This Mean?

Time perception is influenced by many factors:

- **Attention**: When you're focused on time, it seems to pass slower
- **Emotion**: Anxiety makes time feel slower; boredom makes it feel faster
- **Age**: Children often overestimate duration; older adults underestimate
- **Context**: Familiar tasks seem shorter than novel ones

The tendency to **underestimate** may indicate that participants were engaged in the task (time flies when you're having fun!).
:::

## Statistical Test

Is our mean estimate significantly different from 60 seconds?

```{webr-r}
t.test(timewarp$estimate, mu = 60)
```

## Error Distribution

```{webr-r}
ggplot(timewarp, aes(x = error)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 3, fill = "#9b59b6", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#e74c3c", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 3, label = "Perfect estimation",
           hjust = 0, color = "#e74c3c", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Error (seconds from 60)",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Time Estimation Error",
    subtitle = "Positive = overestimate, Negative = underestimate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold")
  )
```

## Line Length Estimation

Let's also look at the spatial estimation data:

```{webr-r}
# Assuming actual line lengths (you'll need to fill in real values)
actual_line1 <- 10  # cm
actual_line2 <- 15  # cm

timewarp <- timewarp |>
  mutate(
    line1_error = line1 - actual_line1,
    line2_error = line2 - actual_line2
  )

# Summary
timewarp |>
  summarise(
    mean_line1 = mean(line1, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_line2 = mean(line2, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_error1 = mean(line1_error, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_error2 = mean(line2_error, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

## Bonus: Individual Differences

Some people consistently over- or under-estimate. Let's visualise this:

```{webr-r}
ggplot(timewarp, aes(x = reorder(id, error), y = error)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = error > 0)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#e74c3c", "FALSE" = "#3498db"),
                    labels = c("Underestimate", "Overestimate")) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = "Participant",
    y = "Error (seconds)",
    title = "Individual Time Estimation Errors",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold")
  )
```

---

::: {.key-finding}
#### Summary

Time perception shows substantial individual differences. Most participants showed a tendency to **underestimate** 60 seconds, consistent with the idea that engaging tasks make time feel like it passes quickly.
:::
